title-group.article-title: Influence of miR-376c-3p/SYF2 Axis on the Progression of Gastric Cancer

contrib-group.aff: Department of Gastroenterology, The Second Hospital of Shandong University, Jinan, China;

permissions.copyright-statement: ASCO-style conversion for internal testing; source rights remain with the original publisher.

abstract.p: MicroRNA-376c-3p was previous reported to have a crucial role in the progression of human cancer. This study was aimed to investigate the influence of microRNA-376c-3p on the proliferation and migration of human gastric cancer cells and the associated mechanism. We explored the expression of microRNA-376c-3p in gastric cancer cells using reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Also, we analyzed the association and biological significance of microRNA-376c-3p and SYF2 pre-mRNA-splicing factor in gastric cancer. MicroRNA-376c-3p expression was found downregulated in gastric cancer cell lines compared to the normal cell line. MicroRNA-376c-3p directly targeted SYF2 and reduced SYF2 expression. Overexpression of microRNA-376c-3p inhibits gastric cancer cell proliferation and migration. Besides that, overexpression of SYF2 abrogates the inhibitory influences on gastric cancer cell behaviors caused by microRNA-376c-3p mimic. These results showed that microRNA-376c-3p inhibits the proliferation and migration of gastric cancer cells via targeting SYF2.
